Residents and community leaders in the Ikorodu High School bus stop area of Odongiyan, Sagamu Road, Ikorodu, Lagos State, have raised concerns over the siting of a gas station directly beneath high-tension power lines, warning that the facility poses a potential danger to lives and property. The residents, who spoke to PUNCH Metro in separate interviews on Monday, urged relevant government agencies to sustain their intervention and ensure that the community was not exposed to an avoidable disaster. The community head, Tajudeen Ojo, said officials of the Lagos State Environmental Protection Agency had directed the owner of the facility to move it away from the high-tension wires during an inspection last Thursday. He said, “On Thursday or Friday, LASEPA officials directed that the gas station should be moved backwards. The owner was also instructed to move it away from the high-tension wires, and he agreed to comply. He was also asked to visit their office for proper documentation.” Explaining why the community did not raise the alarm earlier, despite the structure being almost completed, Ojo said residents were initially unaware that the site was being converted into a gas station. He explained that the property had previously been used for the sale of cement, leading residents to believe that the business would continue. “When the owner started construction, we did not know what he intended to use the site for. They had previously sold bags of cement there, so we assumed they wanted to continue selling cement or iron rods. “However, when the gas tanker was brought to the site, that was when we started raising the alarm and objecting to the project,” he said. A resident, Kazeem Olasupo, said his efforts to sensitise the management of a nearby school about the project led to an altercation in which he and a community leader were allegedly assaulted. Olasupo said he visited the school to inform the principal about the concerns surrounding the facility and encouraged two staff members to attend a meeting with the Lagos State Safety Commission. He said that after the meeting, one of the staff members questioned why he was opposing the business and subsequently informed the person who allocated the land to the gas station operator about where his car was parked. Even the chief Imam of a nearby estate, who intervened to prevent further attacks on me, was also beaten,” he said. On the intervention of LASEPA, Olasupo said the agency had demanded the facility’s regulatory documents, but the operator could not produce any. “The owner did not have a single regulatory document. He simply established something there without the required documentation,” he said. He added that the agency directed the operator to stop work and invited those involved to its headquarters for further engagement. Olasupo, however, expressed concern that moving the facility slightly backwards might not adequately address the danger. “Even if they move the facility further back, it will still pose a danger,” he said. According to him, the community had also challenged the landlord over his decision to lease the property for the project, particularly since the land was allegedly government property. Another resident, Bolarinwa Ojo, said the proposed relocation of the facility by a few centimetres might not sufficiently address the safety concerns, as the gas station was directly beneath the high-tension power lines. He said the suggestion to move the structure backwards was part of the resolution reached during his last engagement with the relevant officials, although he was unaware of any subsequent developments. Ojo also explained that the community was not initially aware of the nature of the project because the arrangement was reached privately between the landowner and the operator. “In fact, I did not know they were constructing a gas station until the structure had been erected. That was when I became aware of what was happening,” he said. He maintained that neither the community head nor the Community Development Association authorised the project, adding that the community only intervened after residents discovered the nature of the business and its potential implications. Ojo said the community would naturally oppose any activity that infringed on residents’ interests or posed a danger to their lives. Meanwhile, the Ikorodu Coordinator of the Committee for the Defence of Human Rights, Oludare Abolurin, said the organisation was monitoring the controversy over the gas station, particularly concerns about regulatory compliance, environmental protection and public safety. In a statement made available to PUNCH Metro on Monday, Abolurin said a LASEPA inspection team, led by an official identified as Engr. Sawyer visited the facility on Thursday, November 5, 2026. He said he and the community head were also present during the inspection, adding that the officials reportedly discovered that the operators could not produce any regulatory document to establish compliance with the relevant approval requirements. “The discovery reportedly came as a shock to the inspection team and has further strengthened calls for a comprehensive regulatory investigation,” the statement read. The CDHR coordinator also raised concerns over alleged threats and intimidation against residents and human rights advocates opposing the project. He said the organisation expected disagreements over community interests to be addressed through lawful and peaceful means. Abolurin further disclosed that the woman associated with the project and her husband had reportedly been invited to appear at LASEPA’s headquarters in Alausa on Monday, November 9, for further engagement. He said the organisation would continue to monitor the situation and engage relevant authorities to ensure accountability and protect residents. “No private commercial interest should be allowed to override established regulatory obligations or the legitimate concerns of a host community,” he added. As of the time of filing this report, the LASEPA stop-work order remained in place at the project site. Uthman Salami Uthman, a Mass Communication graduate from Ahmadu Bello University, Zaria, has over six years experience in journalism. He reports crime to community-related news for Metro, business with a focus on the capital market and the oil and gas.
